page: Amazon Web Services r5n.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. System memory totals 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Cache provisions include 32 KB of L1d, 1.0 MB of L2, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI.

The hardware configuration features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled GPUs, and no local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent filesystem operations. Benchmark results place general processing throughput in the middle 50% tier, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 7702.63, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4604.0, and a stress-ng multi-core score of 6854.52. Single-core throughput ranks lower, with stress-ng single-core compute landing in the bottom 25% at 1304.39.

Memory-intensive metrics align with its architectural focus, delivering 52.94 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth, 40.35 GB/sec in uncached write bandwidth, and 6.61 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Static web throughput measures 6.68 GB/sec. Large language model execution remains constrained by the lack of accelerators, recording 6.03 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

Because the platform couples high memory density with standard compute performance, it yields balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise software rather than pure compute tasks. The r5n.2xlarge is primarily suited for in-memory caches like Redis, medium relational database workloads, in-memory analytics, and backend data processing pipelines.
